description: POSIX-extras primitives exercised through the library/namespace API (no FUSE mount): xattrs, symlinks, hard links, supplementary groups, and durability (fsync vs fdatasync).

checks.expected: the value round-trips as 42
contains the stored name and the derived user.orfs.* set
checks.notes: derived attributes are computed, never stored (docs/NAMESPACE.md §2.2)

checks.expected: a non-empty version string
EEXIST
replaces the value
ENODATA
remove succeeds; a later get or remove returns ENODATA
empty and >255-byte names rejected with EINVAL
read allowed (getxattr/listxattr); write denied (setxattr/removexattr) -> EACCES
checks.notes: src/fuse.rs applies this mask via has_permission_grouped before setxattr/removexattr

checks.expected: names are opaque; no namespace-specific privilege or CAP_SYS_ADMIN override
checks.notes: docs/LIMITATIONS.md §8: one uniform rule, independent of namespace
checks.observed: both stored and returned; the write mask is identical for either prefix

primitives.name: xattrs
primitives.notes: set/get/list/remove, XATTR_CREATE, the derived user.orfs.* set, name bounds, and the uniform access rule.

checks.expected: the new inode is of kind symlink
returns the authoritative target bytes
lookup(target) yields the target inode and its bytes
checks.notes: single-component relative target; multi-component walks are the kernel's
checks.observed: resolved inode == target inode; content = hello

checks.expected: EINVAL (not a symlink)
the link inode replaces the destination; identity and target preserved; the old file is unlinked
checks.observed: victim resolves to the link inode; target still sym-target; old file nlink = 0

checks.expected: EEXIST
checks.what: rename RENAME_NOREPLACE onto an existing name

checks.expected: a second name raises nlink 1 -> 2 and both names resolve to one inode
identical bytes read through either name
nlink 2 -> 1; the remaining name still reads the data; the removed name is ENOENT
checks.observed: nlink = 1; removed name ENOENT; data retained

checks.expected: nlink reaches 0; the inode and its data remain readable by id (append-only tombstone)
checks.notes: docs/NAMESPACE.md §4.2: a tombstone removes a name; the inode/bytes are never withdrawn
checks.observed: nlink = 0; lookup ENOENT; read_at(inode) still returns data

checks.expected: rejected with EPERM (as Linux does)

primitives.name: hard_links
primitives.notes: second link, nlink accounting, shared inode identity, and removal semantics.

checks.expected: owner rw; a supplementary group grants the group read class only; a primary-group match grants it; a stranger is denied; root bypasses
checks.notes: the Linux in_group_p rule; the FUSE transports read Groups: from /proc/<pid>/status

checks.expected: a supplementary group admits the read; without it the read is denied
checks.notes: src/query.rs shares has_permission_grouped with the transports

primitives.name: supplementary_groups
primitives.notes: the grouped permission rule for a supplementary (non-primary) group, allowed and denied.

checks.expected: a successful commit is acknowledged only at TxState::Durable (durable = true)
checks.notes: docs/FUSE-SEMANTICS.md §8.1: fsync/fsyncdir call the engine sync()

checks.expected: ordered commits ack at Published; flush() makes the outstanding batch durable and is idempotent
checks.notes: docs/FUSE-SEMANTICS.md §8.1: fsync calls sync(); flush() is the durability barrier
checks.observed: commit = published/durable=false; flush transactions = 1; second flush = 0

checks.expected: sync() is the single durability entry point; data survives an independent reopen
no distinct primitive; served by the same full sync() (strictly stronger)
checks.notes: no errno: the operation is never rejected, so a reply is never a weaker (wrong) success
checks.observed: the kernel delivers fdatasync(2) as fsync with the datasync hint; src/fuse.rs maps both to core.sync()

primitives.name: durability
primitives.notes: fsync is the durability barrier (ack state Durable vs Published); fdatasync has no distinct primitive and is covered by the same full sync().
